data.why: The app already bundles its own USGS site inventory (nwis_inventory_filtered_data_only.txt) and a WA Dept. of Ecology station catalog CSV (hydrology/data/catalogs/ecology_streamflow_stations.csv) at the repo root/paths the code expects, so no synthetic data needs to be written; actual discharge/climate time series are fetched live from USGS NWIS / Open-Meteo / Meteostat at runtime.

goals: Find a USGS gage of interest on the map and check whether it has recent discharge, stage, and nearby climate data available
Pull a multi-year discharge record for one site and inspect its hydrograph, trend (Mann-Kendall), and flow-duration/frequency diagnostics
Characterize low-flow and drought behavior at a site (baseflow index, flow percentiles, drought indicators)
Compare two sites or two time periods at the same site side-by-side to see how flow regimes differ
Evaluate a river reach for upstream/downstream gain or loss and estimate aquifer contribution

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree of the station-finding, single-site diagnostic and reach gain/loss workflows, and every screen I sampled matches its node. It needs fixes before filing: it leaves out the site-to-site, multi-site, flood-frequency, climate and watershed parts of the interface, and its comparison and reach nodes were never confirmed by the replay.
